correctness.rationale: For the specified symmetric two-mutualist one-substrate Monod system, total mass obeys a linear dissipative bound and the log biomass ratio satisfies d/dt log(x1/x2)=f(S,x2)-f(S,x1), opposite in sign to x1-x2. This rules out nonsymmetric interior periodic orbits and forces equal biomasses at positive equilibria. On x1=x2=x, solving f(S,x)=d yields a strictly convex scalar feed S_in=H(x) with one nondegenerate minimum and 0,1,2 equilibria. The antisymmetric Jacobian eigenvalue is -u where u=xf_x in (0,d); symmetric trace=-D-v+u, determinant=dv-Du, v=2xf_S. Positive determinant and trace>=0 would force (d-D)u>dD, impossible if d<=2D. Thus upper branch stable and no spectral Hopf for d<=2D. For each d>2D an explicit one-parameter positive Monod family has positive determinant, zero trace and nonzero trace derivative, proving spectral Hopf feasibility. At exact (D,d,Sin,K,L,m)=(1,5,11,3/5,19,160) the anti eigenvalue is -19/4, planar pair ±i sqrt(14); an independently reconstructed cubic Hopf normal form gives l1=-40879/532480<0 and transversal stable positive cycles for K<3/5 near threshold with m=100(1+K). Dulac factor 1/(x f) in the symmetric plane gives strictly negative weighted divergence for d<=D, excluding all positive nonconstant periodic orbits. No assertion of absence of large cycles for D<d<=2D.

value.rationale: Separates three mathematically distinct regimes—global nonoscillation at d<=D, local Hopf impossibility at d<=2D and constructive Hopf feasibility above 2D—and supplies an exact supercritical stable-cycle witness. This resolves a genuine interpretation gap in a motivated chemostat model rather than merely substituting equal parameters.

limitations: Sharp d>2D means existence of a spectral Hopf crossing for some positive parameters at each ratio; it does not mean every chemostat with d>2D oscillates. Nonzero cubic coefficient and stable cycles proved at one exact parameter family only.
Global nonoscillation proved for d<=D; large orbits in D<d<=2D not covered; unequal growth functions/biomass removals not covered.
